liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feedback** (3 reviews): Reviewer hears this Feedback as fresh and new-sounding; Reviewer praises a very good long stretch of feedback [3][8][14]
- **And We Bid You Good Night** (2 reviews): Reviewer finds this version of the closer not a great one; Reviewer believes Robert Hunter can be heard singing along on this closer [8][9]
- **Turn On Your Lovelight** (1 other source): The tape cuts in partway through the beginning of this song [1]

## The recordings

- **gd1968-03-31.sbd.miller.108995.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 6 songs; 32 min; rated 1.75/5 by 4 [1]. Said about its sound: After about four minutes the sound improves greatly; the first two songs sound muffled, like a hallway; Sounds like stage microphones, with a lot of audience noise mixed into the soundboard [1][14]
- **gd68-03-31.aud.cotsman.14913.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 3 songs; 12 min; rated 3.44/5 by 9 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says the recording sounds too clear to be an audience tape; Sounds as if it was recorded with microphones on stage [2][6]

## Around the show

- This was the last show of the six-month effort that produced the Anthem of the Sun album [8]
- Charlie Miller noted the songs listed for 3/31/68 actually come from 1/22/68 [10]
- Reviewer is unsure whether this show followed the excellent Carousel performances of the previous two nights [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1968-03-31.sbd.miller.108995.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> (4 Track) Master Reels -> Dat (44.1k) [1]. Also: Date and song order follow Dick's DAT notes; the Caution>Feedback>Good Night sequence matches the 1/22/68 upload [1]
- **gd68-03-31.aud.cotsman.14913.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Andy Lemieux and J Cotsman; source: Audience [2]. Also: Miller placed most of this fragment on his 1/22/68 file per Latvala's notes, then posted a better 3/31/68 copy; Per Deadlists, the exact date of this excerpt is unknown; late March 1968 tapes are often labeled soundboards [2][10]
